sentences.text:
The vs Unknown on 8 August, 2023
 High Court Of Andhra Pradesh At Amaravathi

entities.text: High Court Of Andhra Pradesh At Amaravathi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Main Case No.C.C.Nos.358 & 356 of 2023
 Proceeding Sheet
Sl.No Date Office
 Order

The petitioner had sought payment of compensation by way of allotment of alternative land of the petitioner in lieu of Acres 5.00 cents in Sy.No.1/P of Yendada Village of Visakhapatnam (Rural) Mandal, Visakhapatnam District taken over by the respondents from the petitioner.

This Writ Petition was disposed of on 29.04.2022 by a Learned Single Judge of this Court with a direction to the respondents to initiate proceedings for acquisition of the property in terms of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 or to pay compensation in terms of G.O.Ms.No.259 Revenue (Assn.I)
Department, dated 21.06.2016 or issue TDRs, within a period of eight (08) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this Order.

entities.text: Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner has filed the present Contempt Case being aggrieved by the disobedience of the Orders of the Learned Single Judge by the respondents.
It appears that the respondents had filed Writ Appeal Nos.235 & 236 of 2023 against the orders passed by the Learned Single Judge of this Court in this case and related matters.
These Writ Appeals came to be dismissed by a Division Bench on 26.06.2023.

Sri B.S. Shivaji, learned counsel appearing for the respondents would submit that the respondents are approaching the Hon'ble Supreme Court by way of a SLP against the orders of the Division Bench and seeks time.
The Order of the Division Bench was passed on 26.06.2023 and one and half months have elapsed since then.
Sri B.S. Shivaji, learned counsel for the respondents has not been able to place any material to show that an SLP has been filed before the Hon'ble Supreme Court till today.
In the circumstances, two weeks time is granted.
